title: Eastern Long Island Native Communities
summary: Eastern Long Island includes living Native nations, ancestral homelands, maritime labor histories, land claims, language survivals, and sacred landscapes. Shinnecock, Montaukett, Corchaug, Manhansett, Unkechaug, and neighboring communities belong in relation to one another, not as isolated map points.
content:
Public history often overemphasizes first purchases, forts, or archaeology. A fuller narrative includes survival after dispossession, labor in whaling and fishing, land-defense efforts, cultural centers, powwows, churches, families, and continuing political identity.

Because many eastern places include burials, ceremonial landscapes, or vulnerable archaeological deposits, some stories belong in broad wiki context rather than exact map locations.
